info.name: smallStash API
info.description:
Manual/regression testing against the deployed smallStash HTTP API. See docs/architecture.md and docs/todo.md for the live stack details this collection targets.

## Getting a token (SRP-only app client)

The real app client is SRP-only (see infra/SmallstashStack.java) - Postman can't do the SRP handshake itself. Instead, `ALLOW_ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH` is enabled specifically for manual testing (admin-only flow, requires privileged AWS credentials - never exposed to the public client). Once that CDK change is deployed, mint a token with:

```
aws cognito-idp admin-initiate-auth \
  --user-pool-id eu-west-1_CY70Hunz3 \
  --client-id es8shgod8c4glft5nrn1hennc \
  --auth-flow ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH \
  --auth-parameters USERNAME=test@example.com,PASSWORD='<TEST_USER_PASSWORD - do not commit, see your own local notes>' \
  --region eu-west-1
```

Copy the `AuthenticationResult.AccessToken` value from the response into this collection's `access_token` variable (or the paired environment file's variable). A collection-level pre-request script then reuses it automatically (checks the token's own `exp` claim, no re-fetch needed) for as long as it's valid - it only stops you and prints this same command again once the token's actually expired or missing, instead of blindly re-running it or blindly sending a stale one. See docs/todo.md for why this doesn't auto-fetch a fresh token by itself (would need AWS IAM credentials embedded in Postman - a bigger secret than the JWT itself).

## What's in here

- **Sanity checks**: confirms auth is actually enforced (no token -> 401), not just assumed.
- **Keys**: GET/PUT /keys - the KDF salt/params + wrapped Vault Key metadata (DynamoDB).
- **Vault**: GET/PUT /vault - the whole-vault ciphertext blob (S3).

Request bodies use placeholder base64 values, NOT real Argon2id/AES-GCM output - there's no PWA yet to produce real ciphertext. This collection tests the API/auth/storage plumbing, not the crypto.
